questions.prompt: Why might an attacker deliberately choose VBScript or JScript over PowerShell in an environment with strong PowerShell logging?
options: VBScript is more powerful than PowerShell
Strong PowerShell-specific logging doesn't cover Windows Script Host execution at all — it's a genuine, exploitable blind spot
VBScript is a newer technology than PowerShell
PowerShell can't be used to download files
questions.explanation: This is the core premise of the lesson: an environment that heavily invests in PowerShell logging but ignores Windows Script Host has a real gap attackers specifically route around.

questions.prompt: What makes wscript.exe a preferred delivery mechanism over a visible cmd.exe or PowerShell window?
options: wscript.exe requires administrator privileges to run
wscript.exe runs completely silently by default, with no visible console window
wscript.exe is blocked on all modern Windows versions
questions.explanation: wscript.exe's default silent execution (no console window) makes it far less likely to prompt a user's second look compared to a visible shell window.

questions.prompt: Beyond execution, what persistence mechanism from earlier in this level does WMI also enable?
questions.explanation: The same WMI interface used for remote execution is also how WMI Event Subscription persistence gets established — one interface serving both roles.

questions.prompt: What dedicated event log channel captures WMI method calls independent of standard process-creation logging?
questions.explanation: WMI-Activity/Operational is the dedicated channel that records WMI method calls, including remote ones, that standard process-creation logging alone won't fully capture.
